title: The signal from space that was heard only once
hook: A telescope in Ohio heard a signal from space, once, and never again.
summary: In 1977 Ohio's Big Ear telescope recorded a 72-second radio burst from Sagittarius that was never detected again, and its source is still unknown.
sources: Wikipedia: Wow! signal. Detected 15 August 1977 by Big Ear at Ohio State University, 72 seconds, near 1420 MHz hydrogen line, toward Sagittarius, noticed by Jerry Ehman who wrote 'Wow!'
Ohio History Connection / NASA SETI summaries: signal never detected again; Big Ear demolished in 1998.

lines.text: A telescope in Ohio heard a signal from space, once.
In nineteen seventy-seven, Ohio's Big Ear telescope scanned the sky.
Days later, volunteer Jerry Ehman spotted a strong burst on the printout.
lines.caps: Days *later, | *Jerry Ehman | spotted a *burst | on the *printout

lines.text: He circled it in red and wrote one word: Wow.
It lasted seventy-two seconds, near the frequency of hydrogen.
It came from Sagittarius, but was never heard again.
Nobody knows if it was nature, interference, or a message.
lines.caps: Nobody *knows | if it was *nature, | *interference, | or a *message

lines.text: The telescope was torn down in nineteen ninety-eight.

post.caption:
Seventy-two seconds of radio noise, and nobody has explained it in almost fifty years.
What do you think it was?
